english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is its Measure.
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by a biographical narrative frame (Mani visiting King Shapur, standing on the Tigris quay during flood). The oldest teaching layer — about the First Man assuming elemental garments, the cosmic rulers consuming vast waters, the binding of the mighty giants, and the eschatological dissolution of the material universe — is embedded within this narrative but extractable. The substrate teaching about the measure of the garment of waters is genuine cosmological-correspondential material about cosmic scale and elemental combat. The Tigris flood serves as a pedagogical occasion that the compilers used to frame this teaching. Gardner's note that the chapter's value lies in 'historical reference' confirms that the narrative frame is the editors' contribution. Paragraph 9 is the purest substrate passage. The chapter lacks the systematic zoomorphic/metal/taste mappings seen in Ch. 6 but preserves cosmic process vocabulary (elements, garments, rulers, binding, dissolution).
